newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - LeBow files slate to oust RJR board.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - LeBow files slate to oust RJR board.

text.p: In a move that will pit him against former partner Carl Icahn, investor Bennett LeBow said Tuesday he will try again to oust the board of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
LeBow, who heads holding company Brooke Group Ltd., nominated a nine-man slate that will support an immediate spin-off of RJR's 80.5 percent-owned Nabisco Holdings Corp. subsidiary.
Icahn and LeBow were defeated earlier this year in a joint attempt to pursue the same goals. The controversial investors split shortly after shareholders rejected their efforts in April.
The move by LeBow, who holds about a 1.3 percent stake in RJR, came just one day after Icahn submitted his own slate of board nominees. Icahn holds a 7.3 percent stake in RJR.
LeBow filed his list of nominees on the last day that shareholders are permitted to file board slates for RJR's 1997 annual shareholders meeting.
In addition to LeBow, the slate will include Ronald Fulford, chairman and chief executive officer of Brooke tobacco subsidiary Liggett Group.
Icahn on Monday nominated a slate to be led by Thomas Rattigan, a former executive with PepsiCo Bottling International and G. Heileman Brewing Co.
"We are already in the tobacco business and we have our own views on how to resolve tobacco litigation," a Brooke spokesman said when asked why LeBow nominated his own slate apart from Icahn's.

Earlier this year, Brook Group broke from the rest of the tobacco industry and agreed to settle a class action suit as well as lawsuits from states that are seeking to recoup health care costs of smokers.

RJR confirmed that it received notice of the LeBow slate, but said the action did not merit any comment. The food and tobacco giant has repeatedly said it is committed to a spin-off of Nabisco, but that this is not the appropriate time to split up the company.
Meanwhile, Icahn said the move by LeBow had been expected, stressing that the LeBow slate was completely separate from his nominees.
